newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain's influence would wane outside EMU-Brittan.
newsitem.headline: Britain's influence would wane outside EMU-Brittan.

text.p: A senior European Commission official warned Britain on Thursday that it risked losing its influence in EU economic and political affairs if it stayed outside economic and monetary union.

In prepared remarks released ahead of a speech later today in London, Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, said opting out of a common currency would mean "British interests would carry less weight, as we would not be part of the decision-making core in Europe." (see BC-TEXT-COM-BRITTAN)
The economic costs of such a decision would not be trivial, the British Commissioner added.
"For the markets, a Britain outside EMU would be a greater inflation risk and would have more volatile exchange rates. The markets would demand a price for this," he said.

Taking issue with those who have argued that Britain's economic interests would be best served outside a single currency, the outspoken commissioner said he was not convinced that independence would lead to success.

"I simply do not believe that the anti-inflationary culture of recent years is now so deeply imbedded in the system that it can be relied on to endure without an external link such as an institutionally integrated Central Bank," Brittan added.
Joining monetary union and a European Central Bank would set a tough approach towards monetary policy and eliminate the risks of a policy reversal, he said.
